title: MathMaster server-grading coverage audit (Phase 1)
snapshotOf: main @ a7a3b4e (Merge PR #404), before the server-authoritative grading parity branch
method: 16 independent tracers each read the real code for one group of tools/types/subsystems (no inference), ran probes where a claim needed a value, and recorded one entry per tool/type/meaningful mode. A completeness critic and adversarial verifiers then re-checked the high-impact findings. Line numbers refer to the snapshot. Eight entries were reclassified by the critic (each carries classificationCorrection) and six surfaces it found were added (auditGroup "critic"). The adversarial verifications are in "verifications"; none of the eight findings was refuted.
readMe: This file is the frozen BEFORE state. The AFTER state is declared in functions/shared/serverGrading/gradingManifest.mjs and rendered into docs/architecture/SERVER_GRADING_COVERAGE.md by scripts/report-server-grading-coverage.mjs.

entries.studentFacing: Free-order 'Multiple representations' board (RepresentationBridge.jsx:46-47 delegates to LinearMultipleRepresentationsBoard.jsx:467). A GIVEN panel renders the authored source read-only (describeGivenRepresentation, linearMultipleRepresentationsMath.js:1793-1848; kinds standardForm|slopeIntercept|pointSlope|twoPoints|table|graph|scenario). The student builds every other representation in any order, nothing gated (DEFAULT_EXPANDED, Board.jsx:150-158). CARDS (only those in resolveRequiredCards, Board.jsx:470; the GIVEN card is removed): Equations panel: Standard form (MathInput 'equation', Board.jsx:972), Slope-intercept (973), Point-slope (974). Key features: Slope (MathInput 'number', 978), x-intercept and y-intercept (MathInput 'orderedPair', 979-980), Two points (two 'orderedPair' inputs, 984-1014). Table: plain text x/y cells, 4 blank rows by default, unbounded '+ Add row', and row remove (1016-1095). Graphs: three separate CoordinatePlanes. Graph 1 is the intercept method, Graph 2 slope-intercept, Graph 3 point-slope with its anchor guide (GRAPHS 160-182). Each takes at most 2 snapped points: a third tap replaces the second (plotPoint 733-739). Drag, undo and start over are available (1097-1142), plus an enlarge dialog. 'What the numbers mean' panel (1199-1224): shows each context field whose key is authored. It is a <select> when a choice bank exists, the domain uses MathInput 'inequality', otherwise a text input. Per-card Check buttons appear only when feedbackTiming==='guided' AND runtime showImmediateFeedback is on (Board.jsx:474-476). DOL/submitOnly shows only fill progress. 'Submit board' asks for confirmation when any required card or context field is empty, then submits once (882-888, 1417-1437). After submit, feedback shows the % correct, the parts to revisit and the consistency outliers (1439-1467).
entries.browserGrading: Final grade: LinearMultipleRepresentationsBoard.jsx:863-881 doSubmit() calls scoreLinearMultipleRepresentations(questionData, responseRef.current) (linearMultipleRepresentationsMath.js:1577-1686). That re-derives canonicalFacts from question.source via deriveLinearMultipleRepresentations (470-580), records one boolean part per required card, per authored context field and for crossRepresentationConsistency. It then computes score = correctCount/parts.length and isCorrect = every(part) (1673-1676). PER CARD (part key, raw field, grader): (1) standardForm, standardFormEquation, validateStandardFormEntry (919-981). Steps: latexToExpression; exactly one '='; isLinearStandardFormEquation structural check (algebraAstEngine.js:918); standardCoefficientsFromEquationText (linearEquations.js:112-133, which evaluates with mathjs at sample points); integer coefficients (1e-4); gcd==1; A>0 (or A==0 and B>0); canonicalFromStandard + linesEquivalent(1e-6). (2) slopeIntercept, slopeInterceptEquation, validateSlopeInterceptEntry (988-1028). Left side must be the mathjs SymbolNode y; right side must pass isSimplifiedSlopeInterceptExpression (algebraAstEngine.js:780: at most 2 terms, reduced coefficients); then canonicalFromEquationText + linesEquivalent(1e-6). (3) pointSlope, pointSlopeEquation, validatePointSlopeEntry (1038-1074). parsePointSlopeForm is a mathjs AST matcher (360-412) for y-y1=m(x-x1), -(x-x1) and (x-x1)/d. The slope must match within 1e-4, the point must lie on the line (1e-6) and the lines must be equivalent. Any point on the line is accepted. (4) slope, featureSlope, validateSlopeEntry (1080-1090): parseNumericOrFraction (184-206, LaTeX \frac -> a/b, decimals allowed), then matchesNumericAnswer with tolerance 1e-4. (5) xIntercept, featureXIntercept, validateXInterceptEntry (1119-1130): parseOrderedPair (1092-1117), y≈0 and x≈zeroNumber, both within 1e-4. (6) yIntercept, featureYIntercept, validateYInterceptEntry (1132-1143), same rules. (7) twoPoints, featurePoint1 + featurePoint2, validateTwoPointsEntry (1145-1161): points distinct and both on the line (1e-6). Not graded when source.kind==='twoPoints'. (8) table, tableRows, validateTableEntry(rows, facts, 4) (1163-1202): at least 4 rows; EVERY row must parse (a trailing blank row fails the card); x-values distinct; each row on the line (1e-6). Not graded when source.kind==='table'. (9) graph1, graph1Points, evaluateGraph1Intercepts (1208-1216): graphing2/constructionPolicy.js evaluateConstruction, formAware with requiredAnchor 'intercepts'. Anchors are the x- and y-intercepts derived from canonicalFacts.standard; tolerance = question.tolerance||0.12 (1688-1691). (10) graph2, graph2Points, evaluateGraph2SlopeIntercept (1218-1226): anchor is the y-intercept, plus one more on-line point. (11) graph3, graph3Points, resolveGraph3Anchor(question, facts, response.pointSlopeEquation) (1396-1406) then evaluateGraph3PointSlope (1439-1470). The anchor is the GIVEN point when source.kind==='pointSlope'. Otherwise it is the point from the student's point-slope equation if that point is on the line. Otherwise mode is free, where the first plotted point within 1.5*tol of the line becomes the anchor. (12) Context fields contextIndependent, contextDependent, contextSlopeMeaning, contextYInterceptMeaning, contextXInterceptMeaning: validateContextField (1232-1259), a normalized string-equality match against expected. Expected can be a string, an array or {acceptedAnswers, value, answer, choices}. Each field is graded iff (source.context||context)[key]!=null (1617-1642). (13) contextDomain: validateDomainField (1311-1383) with parseInequalityDomain (1261-1309). Expected is question.domain||ctx.domain (1643-1648). (14) crossRepresentationConsistency: checkCrossRepresentationConsistency (1476-1575). It builds a line from each filled equation, from the table (at least 2 valid rows, collinear), from the two points (the given points when source is twoPoints, 1650-1652) and from each graph's first 2 points. It passes iff all pairs satisfy linesEquivalent, and it is vacuously TRUE when fewer than 2 lines exist (1536-1538). It is ALWAYS graded. Per-card guided Check (formative only): validateCard (Board.jsx:602-621) and judgeContext (661-667) call the SAME validators. Verdicts are recomputed from fingerprints (checkedCards, 650-657) and are never stored. EXACT FRACTIONS: the canonical line is stored as exact rationals {n,d} (linearEquations.js toFraction 39-48), and display uses exact LaTeX (fractionLatex 1698). Student comparisons, however, use float tolerances: slope, intercepts and the point-slope m use 1e-4, so a slope of '0.3333' is accepted for 1/3 (verified by running it). Equations, table and two points use 1e-6, so y=0.3333x+1 is rejected (verified). requiredCards: resolveRequiredCards (121-127) expands categories (equationForms/features/table/graphs, DEFAULT_BOARD_CATEGORIES 50-55) and always drops the GIVEN card (GIVEN_CARD_BY_KIND 101-107; graph and scenario sources have no given card). Context parts and the consistency part are graded regardless of requiredCards.

entries.rawResponseRequired: Student state (all already in the board's response object, Board.jsx:529-553): standardFormEquation, slopeInterceptEquation, pointSlopeEquation (MathLive LaTeX strings); featureSlope, featureXIntercept, featureYIntercept, featurePoint1, featurePoint2 (LaTeX strings); tableRows (array of {x:string, y:string}, ALL rows, because any unparseable row fails the table); graph1Points, graph2Points, graph3Points (array of at most 2 finite [x,y] number pairs; the first two also feed the consistency check); contextIndependent, contextDependent, contextSlopeMeaning, contextYInterceptMeaning, contextXInterceptMeaning, contextDomain (strings). Question state (server-held): source, requiredCards, tolerance, context/source.context, domain. NOT needed: snapStep, graphBounds, feedbackTiming, checkedCards, expandedCards, undo history, showImmediateFeedback. The grade does NOT depend on any client state missing from the emitted response. The Graph 3 anchor comes from response.pointSlopeEquation plus question.source, and graph tolerance comes from the question.
entries.rawResponseEmittedToday: Board.jsx:876-880: submit({ isCorrect: result.isCorrect, score: result.score }, response, { parts, evidence: result.evidence, canonicalFacts: result.canonicalFacts }). response = responseRef.current, the exact 18-field object above. tableRows defaults to 4 blank rows ([{x:'',y:''}x4]) and the graph point arrays may be empty. parts (869-875) = [{id: 'standardForm'|'slopeIntercept'|'pointSlope'|'slope'|'xIntercept'|'yIntercept'|'twoPoints'|'table'|'graph1'|'graph2'|'graph3'|'contextIndependent'|...|'contextDomain'|'crossRepresentationConsistency', label: PART_LABELS[id], isComplete: true (always, even when blank), isCorrect: bool, response: ''}]. evidence holds each validator's output keyed by part. It includes the graph anchors' CORRECT intercept points even when the student is wrong (verified: anchors [{id:'xIntercept',point:[9,0]},{id:'yIntercept',point:[0,18]}]), graph3 anchorPoint, and consistency disagreements/outliers. canonicalFacts is the complete derived key: canonicalLine, slope, intercepts, xInterceptPoint, yInterceptPoint, standard, standardEquation, slopeInterceptEquation, sourcePoint, twoPoints, source, and context including the .value answers. useToolSubmission.js:7-11 forwards {...result, response, metadata} to onAction('ATTEMPT_SUBMITTED'). QuestionEngine.jsx:754-781 (ordinary mode) uses only payload.isCorrect, payload.score (as partialCreditPercent), metadata.parts and JSON.stringify(payload.response) as responseKey. evidence and canonicalFacts are dropped there. Under serverGrading (738-752) only payload.response is sent.
entries.answerKeyFields: Line key, inherently public because it is the GIVEN representation: question.source.kind plus one of source.equation | A,B,C | m,b | point(+m) | points or first/second | rows | line{m,b} | rate,initialValue. The scenario prompt is source.prompt/text. Context key, secret but currently shipped to the client: (question.source.context || question.context).{independentQuantity, dependentQuantity, slopeMeaning, yInterceptMeaning, xInterceptMeaning}, each one of {value | answer | acceptedAnswers[] | choices[]}, a string or an array. Domain key: question.domain || context.domain, given as [min,max] | {min,max,minInclusive,maxInclusive,value,choices,acceptedAnswers} | string. Grading configuration: requiredCards, tolerance. Display only (not grading): choiceBanks/choices lists, snapStep, graphBounds, feedbackTiming. Stored Firestore shape: two-point and graph source points become [{x,y}], and authoredPointPair (446-450) and readSourceTableRows (427-437) already accept both shapes.
entries.partialCredit: Yes, legitimately. All parts have equal weight. score = (# true parts)/(# parts), where the parts are the required card parts, plus the authored context parts, plus crossRepresentationConsistency (always present). Sample counts: 11 parts for lmr-cw-1/2/3 and lmr-pr-1 (10 cards + consistency), 18 for lmr-pr-2 (11 cards + 6 context + 1), 10 for lmr-dol-1 (6 cards + 3 context + 1). Graph evaluations compute an internal fractional score (constructionPolicy.js), but only isCorrect is used per part. QuestionEngine turns score into partialCreditPercent (QuestionEngine.jsx:768-771). recordQuestionAttempt caps non-correct credit at 90 and takes the max with the part-weighted percent.
entries.envelopeCarriesEnough: partial. App.jsx:5677-5680 builds ordinarySubmission.response = normalizeCheckpointResponse(question, {parts, responseKey}), which gives normalizeOrdinaryResponse (ordinaryResponseGrading.mjs:272-293) = {kind:'opaque', type:'representationBridge', value: responseKey.slice(0,2000), fields:[]}. responseKey is JSON.stringify of all 18 raw fields, so for typical boards it IS complete: a fully correct 18-part candle board measured 840 chars, and 12 rows with fractional snap points measured 1058. But table rows are unbounded ('+ Add row') and JSON doubles LaTeX backslashes. 30 \frac rows reached 1995 chars, and anything longer is silently cut into unparseable JSON. The envelope carries no mode or schema version (mode lives only on the stored question). parts carry response:'' so they hold no per-part work. The server ignores this payload today anyway (unsupported-type). Separately, the raw fields also reach the server through the workspace draft record '<draftKey>:work:tool' (usePersistentToolState toolDraftKey, 16 KB cap, workspaceDraftSchema.mjs:25).

entries.blockers: 1. No server grader: 'representationBridge' is not in SERVER_GRADEABLE_QUESTION_TYPES (ordinaryResponseGrading.mjs:42-48), and hasAnswerKey (57-72) has no case for it. The tool has two modes ('linear' and 'linearMultipleRepresentations', representationBridgeMath.js:34) with different response shapes, so the server must dispatch on question.mode. 2. mathjs dependency: the grader chain imports mathjs in 4 files (linearMultipleRepresentationsMath.js:9, shared/linearEquations.js:15, algebraAstEngine.js:1, algebraExactRational.js:17), and functions/package.json has none. The structural form checks are mathjs-AST-coupled (isLinearStandardFormEquation, isSimplifiedSlopeInterceptExpression, parsePointSlopeForm). algebraicForm.mjs parsePolynomial could replace only the coefficient extraction (standardCoefficientsFromEquationText). Parity requires pinning the same mathjs major version as root (^15.2.0), because implicit-multiplication precedence ('1/2x') decides slope-intercept verdicts. 3. Transport: the opaque 2000-char slice of responseKey can truncate (unbounded table rows), and nothing carries a schema/mode. A bounded structured response kind is needed. 4. No live answerState from registry tools, so checkpoint/deadline finalization cannot work without a new tool-to-QuestionEngine response channel, or without reading the workspace draft. 5. Answer keys ship to the client: context.*.value/acceptedAnswers and domain min/max/value are in questionData because the board renders choices and runs guided Check locally. A server-authoritative design needs a key-stripped student projection for these. The line itself cannot be hidden, because the GIVEN source defines it. 6. Grading quirks to settle before freezing parity (all verified by running them): a blank board earns crossRepresentationConsistency (blank score 0.091 for lmr-cw-1..pr-1, 0.056 for pr-2, 0.100 for dol-1); one trailing blank table row fails the whole table card; slope/intercepts accept 4-decimal approximations (1e-4) while the equations require 1e-6; the board's Check uses questionData.domain ?? ctx.domain (Board.jsx:590) while the scorer uses question.domain || ctx.domain (math.js:1644). 7. The persisted partial credit comes from the client score: recordQuestionAttempt (attemptPolicy.mjs:480-486) takes max(part percent, supplied percent), capped at 90.

entries.mode: linear (also mode omitted; any mode other than 'linearMultipleRepresentations' renders and grades this path). feedbackTiming guided | checkpoint (default) | submitOnly changes only when Submit is enabled and whether per-stage checks show; it does not change the grading function.
entries.studentFacing: One linear relationship from an authored table, shown in five connected panels. (1) Table/rate: pick two rows, type Δx, Δy and Δy/Δx, record at least requiredComparisons distinct intervals, choose 'The rate is constant' or 'not constant', and type m. (2) General form: type m, b and a 'y = mx + b' equation. (3) Factored form: type a, c and a 'y = a(x − c)' equation. (4) Graph: plot 2 points on a CoordinatePlane (x-intercept anchor plus a slope point; a 3rd click starts over). (5) Meaning: for m, b and c, pick a unit, a contextual meaning and a mathematical role from choice banks. In guided and checkpoint timing, each stage has an unlimited 'Check this stage' button with a correct / needs-another-look pill. In checkpoint timing, 'Submit the bridge' stays disabled until every required stage is checked and still passing (RepresentationBridge.jsx:257-258). In guided and submitOnly, Submit is always enabled, including on a blank board.
entries.browserGrading:
RepresentationBridge.jsx:101 sets liveResult = scoreRepresentationBridge(questionData, response) on every edit. check() at :260-266 submits {isCorrect: liveResult.isCorrect, score: liveResult.score}. The grading lives in representationBridgeMath.js:190-289.
- deriveLinearBridge (:73-82) fits m and b with fitTableLine over normalizeRows(source.rows) and sets zero = -b/m.
- rateEvidence (:201-230): every recorded interval's dx, dy and rate must match intervalTruth within 1e-6 via matchesNumericAnswer; there must be at least requiredComparisons distinct pairs and no duplicates; studentSlope must be within 1e-4 of m; rateConclusion must be 'constant'.
- generalForm (:233-246): m and b within 1e-4; structurallyValidForm(equation, 'slopeIntercept') via rewriteLinearFormMath buildInitialEquationState/describeRewriteGap; equationEquivalentToTrue via linearEquations canonicalFromEquationText/linesEquivalent.
- factoredForm (:249-258): the same checks with a ≈ m, c ≈ zero and 'factoredLinear'.
- graph (:261-269): evaluateConstruction(points, graphQuestionFor(...) = {mode:'factoredLinear', factored:{a:m, c:zero}, constructionPolicy:{strategy:'formAware', requiredAnchor:'xIntercept'}}, target, tolerance ?? 0.12).
- meaning (:271-276): scoreExpressionMeaning(bridgeMeaningQuestion(question)), an exact normalized string match on 3 concepts × 3 dimensions.
- crossRepresentationConsistency (:278-282): the student's own parseable general, factored and graph lines must be the same line. It is vacuously true when fewer than 2 parse.
- score = true parts / all parts; isCorrect = every part true (:284-286).
QuestionEngine.jsx:756-767 turns the metadata.parts object into parts [{id, label:id, isComplete:true, isCorrect, response:''}], and :768-771 turns score into partialCreditPercent.

- context.rateUnit, outputUnit, inputUnit, rateMeaning, yInterceptMeaning, zeroMeaning: the meaning key (:129-152).

entries.partialCredit:
Yes. score = (true parts)/(all parts), over the required stages plus crossRepresentationConsistency (representationBridgeMath.js:284-286). QuestionEngine also sends each part with isComplete:true, so attemptPolicy's earnedPartPercent equals the same ratio, capped at 90 (attemptPolicy.mjs:477-486). Grade credit = bestPartialCredit/100 (:559-563).

In checkpoint timing (the default), Submit is only possible once every required stage passes, so a submission is effectively always 100%. Guided and submitOnly allow any state, including blank (the 17% / 50% defect).

The per-stage checks are unlimited, consume no attempt, and ignore showImmediateFeedback (QuestionEngine.jsx:979).
entries.envelopeCarriesEnough:
Partial. App.jsx:5677-5680 → normalizeOrdinaryResponse produces {kind:'opaque', type:'representationBridge', value: JSON.stringify(response).slice(0,2000), fields:[]} (ordinaryResponseGrading.mjs:287-292).
- Typical items fit: 765 chars for the 4-row booth-fee fixture with 3 intervals; 1858 chars for an 8-row table with all 28 intervals (both measured).
- No input has a maxLength, and validation sets no upper limit on rows. Long typed equations, more intervals, or long authored meaning strings push past 2000, and the slice then leaves invalid JSON.
- No server code parses an opaque value today.
- mode and requiredStages are not in the envelope, but they are on the stored question.

entries.studentFacing: The student sees an equation (equationLatex, or a generated `y = mx ± b`) and, optionally, a graph. They type the slope m and the y-intercept b into two <input type=number> boxes. Feedback colors each box from feedback.partGrades.
entries.browserGrading: src/GraphLine.jsx:9 destructures {m, b} from the question. GraphLine.jsx:20-25 builds the parts: slope isCorrect = slope !== '' && Number(slope) === m, and intercept isCorrect = Number(intercept) === b. The comparison is exact, with no tolerance and no fraction input. isComplete is true when both boxes are filled; isCorrect is true when isComplete and every part is correct. Reported by onStateChange at GraphLine.jsx:27-29, then QuestionEngine.performSubmit (QuestionEngine.jsx:646-716) calls onGrade(answerState.isCorrect, questionDetails, parts, supportUsage, responseKey, {partialCreditPercent: null}) at :673-683, and App.handleGradeSubmit -> recordQuestionAttempt (App.jsx:5511-5537). The catalogued `answer` field is never read.
entries.browserGraderPurity: The math is two inline Number() equality checks inside a React component (GraphLine.jsx imports react, MathDisplay, QuestionPrompt, GraphDisplay, QuestionVisual, useUndoHistory). There is no separate pure module, but the logic has no dependencies at all.

(2) CONTRACT MISMATCH: the catalog example (questionTypeCatalog.mjs:'graphing') and the V5 compile (authoringIntentV5Core.js:1260-1262) emit {graph, answer, responseType} and never m/b. GraphLine then compares against undefined, so V5- or catalog-authored graphing items can never be marked correct, and the question asks for slope and intercept while the key is a single `answer`. A server grader must define the key: m/b, or derive it from graph.functions[0] {type:'line', m, b}, or `answer`. (3) Generated m/b exist only in the browser.

entries.mode: construct (default: points -> Check -> freehand curve snap -> end markers), incl. studentChoosesX and undefined-probe tasks
entries.studentFacing: The student places each point task on the plane: key point, P1..P5, optional 'Undefined' probes, and their own x-values when studentChoosesX, which V5 defaults to true (authoringIntentV5Core.js:1283). 'Check Point Placements' unlocks drawing only when every point is correct. The student then draws a freehand curve that 'snaps' to the true function and drags arrow/open/closed markers to each graph end, then presses Submit.
entries.browserGrading: In InteractiveGraphWorkspace.jsx:650-671 the parts are: (a) pointParts = gradePointPlacements(tasks, placements, functionSpec, chosenXValues, max(0.22, snapStep*0.48)) (:521; interactiveGraphEngine.js:96-121, which resolves expectations through resolveTaskExpected, enforces distinct and balanced chosen x-values, and handles 'undefined'), each AND-ed with construction.pointsValidated; (b) 'graph-curve' = construction.snapped, a boolean the browser set at :983-985 after roughSketchMatchesGraph over screen-space strokes; (c) markerParts (:619-627), where placement counts as correct if typeof placement==='string' OR placement.locationCorrect===true OR distance(point, requirement.point) ≤ max(0.55, snapStep*1.8), and type counts as correct if marker === requirement.marker. isComplete = pointsValidated && snapped && allMarkersPlaced, and isCorrect = complete && every part correct. Tasks come from question.pointTasks or buildInteractivePointTasks (:343). Endpoint requirements come from question.endpointRequirements or getDefaultEndpointRequirements(functionSpec, sampleVisibleFunctionPaths(...)) (:430).
entries.browserGraderPurity: Partly pure. interactiveGraphEngine.js is pure but imports functionGraphUtils.js, which imports platform/workflow/modelExpression.js, which imports mathjs (compile/parse; used only when functionSpec.type==='expression'). graphInteractionPrecision.js is pure (resolveReachableSnapStep sets snapStep and therefore the tolerances). A later regrade from the stored record can therefore differ for very long answers. The 2000-char opaque responseKey of normalizeOrdinaryResponse is not involved here. NO for tool-contract items: the player cannot collect tool work at all.
entries.questionFamilyCompat: Not the assignment Question Family system. Blueprint targets name Path bank families (pathQuestionBank document ids or bundled seeds; resolveBlueprintFamilies). The server instantiates them with a seedKey from the stored issuancePlan (pathQuestionGeneration via mathPath.instantiateQuestion) and stores the instance and privateGrading on the session before display. No pin rebuild is needed. questionFamilyGrading.mjs is not used.
entries.deadlineFinalizationCompat: Server-native. finalizeSecureExam(reason 'timeExpired') checks the server deadline (secureExam.isExpired, secureExam.js:65-73) and grades the open autosaved draft with the same gradeResponse (index.js 13835-13855, 13800-13832). Proctor forceSubmit does the same (13947). Unanswered planned slots score 0 because weightedSessionScorePercent divides by the plan.
entries.recoveryCompat: Outside Section Recovery: sectionRecovery*.mjs has no Test Cycle hooks. Remediation is the cycle's own Corrections -> secure Retest with a capped contribution (testCycleGrade.mjs). Ordinary submissionIngestion forbids client envelopes carrying testCycle/testCycleGrades (submissionIngestion.mjs:84-94).
entries.blockers: (1) CRITICAL, verified by probe. Tool-contract families (algebra, system, systemsWorkspace, dataModelingLab, regressionCalculator, graphing2, relationMapping, intervalNumberLine, stepAlgebra, functionInvestigation, multiAnswer) pass testCycleFamilyIssuability, because buildTemplateIssuePlan -> buildIssuePlan returns issuable:true for any contract tool (mathPath.js 571-583). The secure delivery then strips the tool: secureExamPublicQuestion calls buildSanitizedQuestion(question, question), and that options object has no `toolPayload` key because the payload was spread onto the question (index.js 13462-13467, 15297; mathPath.js 422-433). The student sees a bare 'Answer' box. Grading then calls gradeResponse, which reads privateGrading.fields, but tool privateGrading is {pathToolId, definition} (pathToolContracts.mjs:1380-1384), so every answer gets {isCorrect:false, score:0}. (2) Per-field choices (94 field-graded seed items) render as free-text inputs, because SecureExamQuestionPlayer.jsx:54 only uses question.choices and only when fields.length===1. The key is an opaque runtime id, so these items cannot be answered. (3) Blueprint target.toolId is carried as metadata only (testCycleIssuance.mjs:164) and is never enforced or rendered. (4) The TEST_CYCLE_ARCHITECTURE claim 'Every declared family can be privately graded' is a false positive for tool families.

QuestionEngine.handleMissingToolAction (QuestionEngine.jsx:729-794) does not grade; it forwards the tool's opinion: (1) Boolean(payload.isCorrect) (775). (2) parts from payload.metadata.parts (756-767). An array maps to {id, label, isComplete, isCorrect, response}. An object map {id: bool} maps to {id, label:id, isComplete:true, isCorrect:Boolean(v), response:''}. (3) partialCreditPercent = round(score<=1 ? score*100 : score), clamped 0..100 (768-771). (4) responseKey = JSON.stringify(payload.response ?? {}) (772). App.jsx handleGradeSubmit then runs recordQuestionAttempt (functions/shared/attemptPolicy.mjs:404-534). That sets status, attemptCount and partialCredit; an incorrect answer's credit is capped at 90 (attemptPolicy.mjs:478,482).

entries.rawResponseRequired: The tool's whole response object. In addition, any work state the tool's own verdict reads that today lives only in metadata or component state: verification flags, reduction lineage, derivation history, plotted strokes and similar. This is decided per tool.
entries.rawResponseEmittedToday: payload = {isCorrect, score, response, metadata} (useToolSubmission.js:8). In the ordinary path only these leave QuestionEngine: isCorrect (boolean), parts (from metadata.parts), responseKey (JSON string of response) and partialCreditPercent. All other metadata is dropped and never crosses the boundary. That metadata is often answer-key material, for example: IntervalNumberLine {checks, expected} :592-596; InverseCompositionLab expected:{fog,gof,inverseAtFx,expectedRestriction} :66-70; DataModelingLab expectedModel/expectedPrediction/regression :295-306; RepresentationMatch expectedId :191-195; Graphing2 target :193-206.
entries.answerKeyFields: At the seam: the tools' metadata (expected, expectedModel, expectedPrediction, expectedId, target, regression, canonicalFacts, correctPairs). It is dropped before the boundary. The authored keys inside questionData are per tool.
entries.partialCredit: Yes. score becomes partialCreditPercent and is combined (max) with part-weighted credit from metadata.parts; incorrect credit is capped at 90 in the browser (attemptPolicy.mjs:478,482). The server sanitizer clamps the claimed partialCredit only to 0..100, not 90 (submissionIngestion.mjs:486).
entries.envelopeCarriesEnough: No. The response object reaches the server only as JSON text. (a) response.value is kind 'opaque', sliced to 2000 chars (ordinaryResponseGrading.mjs:287-292); a probe with a 4826-char tool response kept 2000 chars that no longer JSON.parse. (b) record.lastResponseKey is the untruncated string (attemptPolicy recordQuestionAttempt lastResponseKey; never sliced on the server). toolId and mode are not carried; only question.type is. metadata beyond parts is gone.
entries.questionFamilyCompat: Only through assignment-local family templates whose type is a registry id (questionFamilyTemplate.mjs:184,234-243; toolId survives buildFamilyQuestion because TEMPLATE_ONLY_FIELDS omits it, questionFamilyEngine.mjs:400,423-426). The pin is carried and the server rebuilds the instance, but it cannot grade it, so the client verdict is sanitized. Pre-Flight warns (questionGenerationPreflight.js:117-120,190-192).
entries.deadlineFinalizationCompat: None. Registry tools never call onStateChange, so answerState stays EMPTY_ANSWER_STATE (QuestionEngine.jsx:81-87,302). checkpointPending (456-467) is then always false and no checkpoint is ever written. checkpointEligibility would refuse it anyway (responseCheckpoint.js:37-38).
entries.recoveryCompat: None. sectionRecoveryReadiness.mjs:89 fails with TOOL_NOT_SERVER_GRADABLE, and gradeFamilyInstanceResponse has no tool branch (questionFamilyGrading.mjs:153-159).
entries.blockers: 1) No structured response crosses the boundary: JSON text, truncated to 2000 chars. 2) metadata the verdict depends on is dropped. 3) No per-tool grader in functions/shared for the ordinary path, and serverGradingSupport and gradeOrdinaryResponse are type-switches that know no tools. 4) The delivered question can differ from the stored one: QuestionEngine's runtime repair (algebraWorkspaceRoute.js:248-252, e.g. stepAlgebra2 to stepAlgebra, questionToolContract.js:142), student support transforms (studentSupport.js:157-171 trims choices) and variants/adaptive bands, none of which the server reproduces (functions/lib/assignmentRuntime.js:3-16). 5) handleMissingToolAction has no submissionInFlightRef guard, unlike performSubmit (QuestionEngine.jsx:646-649 vs 737).

entries.studentFacing: This is a server path that re-grades or credits saved student attempts, and the matrix has no entry for it. When a teacher commits a question repair or a Content-version upgrade, migrateTrackerForContentUpgrade rewrites gradesByAssignment and asks for a Classroom section-grade reconcile. It uses its own graders. (a) gradingExpansion on dataModelingLab lineFit/linearFit/linearFitPrediction: it re-runs a private regression with its own tolerances (slope max(0.2,|m|*0.12), intercept 0.8) on the client-written record.lastResponseKey {m,b}. These tolerances are a third set, separate from DataModelingLab.jsx and pathDataModelingGrading.mjs. It sets status 'correct' and credit 100 on the fit alone and ignores the prediction part, which the browser requires for linearFitPrediction and for lineFit with predictionX. (b) gradingExpansion on multiAnswer: it uses its own fieldAccepts (exact normalized text, or numeric only when field.tolerance is set). This is a fourth field matcher, separate from matchesFieldAnswer. It grades the client-supplied partGrades[].response. (c) safeResponseControl: it marks every complete-but-wrong affected part correct with no regrade at all. (d) systemsWorkspaceUpgrade: it gives an attempt back to students whose question had expired. Classification: server-authoritative, with its own unverified graders that read client-written inputs. Node probe: record {status:'attempted', lastResponseKey:{m:1.99,b:0.05,predictionY:-999}} with a linearFitPrediction afterQuestion (points ~y=2x) migrates to status 'correct', bestPartialCredit 100.

entries.studentFacing: This is a separate Google Classroom grade with its own formula, and the matrix has no entry for it. The myMathPath entry covers only per-item grading. The publishWeeklyPathGrades schedule and runWeeklyPathClassroomSyncNow call runWeeklyPathClassroomSync, then weeklyPathSync, then gradeWeeklyGoal (completion 0.8 + quality 0.2, full-completion floor 80), then Classroom patchGrade. The slot's DOK and band then become the preferred band/DOK for issued questions, which feeds the quality/accuracy term. Classification: server-authoritative over a student-chosen task mix.

crossCuttingFindings.finding: SECURITY (latent): the LMR board's submit metadata carries the full answer key. metadata.canonicalFacts holds the canonical line, slope, intercepts, standardEquation, slopeInterceptEquation, source and context with the .value answers. metadata.evidence includes the graph anchors' correct intercept points even for wrong work (LinearMultipleRepresentationsBoard.jsx:879). Today it is dropped: QuestionEngine.jsx:756-781 reads only metadata.parts, and Path sends only payload.response. The FORBIDDEN_ENVELOPE_FIELDS denylist (submissionIngestion.mjs:84-94) would NOT catch canonicalFacts, standardEquation or context.*.value if a future change forwarded metadata. Recommend removing canonicalFacts from the submit metadata, or moving envelope/response validation to an allowlist.

Answer keys ship to the browser. The context meaning answers (context.*.value/acceptedAnswers) and domain (min/max/value) are in the student-delivered questionData because the board renders the choice banks and runs guided Check client-side. No student-safe question projection exists (grep for strip/redact helpers found none). The line-based cards cannot be secret by design, because the GIVEN source defines the line, but the meanings and domain could be.

Registry tools never report live answerState to QuestionEngine. QuestionEngine.jsx:1004 passes only onAction, not commonModuleProps.onStateChange (936). So deadline checkpoints (App.jsx ~5450) cannot capture any registry tool's work even after a grader exists. Two options: add a tool-to-engine response channel, or let the finalizer read the synced workspace draft '<draftKey>:work:tool', which already holds the full raw state for LMR.

Transport: every registry tool submission is reduced to an opaque responseKey.slice(0,2000) (ordinaryResponseGrading.mjs:287-292), with no schema version or mode. For tools with unbounded collections (LMR tableRows), truncation yields unparseable JSON. Server grading for registry tools needs a bounded structured response kind that rejects over-limit input rather than truncating.

Server-graded registry tools need mode dispatch. representationBridge has two modes ('linear' and 'linearMultipleRepresentations', representationBridgeMath.js:34, scoreRepresentationBridge 190-193) with different response shapes. A type-only gate in serverGradingSupport is insufficient.

mathjs parity risk: if graders move to functions/ by adding mathjs, the functions dependency must match root (^15.2.0). The browser verdicts depend on mathjs parse semantics: implicit multiplication such as 'y = 1/2x - 3' is accepted in tests (linearMultipleRepresentations.test.mjs:430), and AST node types drive the structural form checks.

functions/shared/pathGraphingGrading.mjs mirrors only graphing2's legacy equivalent-line grading: no formAware constructionPolicy, line tolerance m 0.08 and b 0.16 versus the browser's linesEquivalent(tolerance). It cannot be reused for LMR Graph 1/2/3, which require intercept, y-intercept and point anchors (constructionPolicy.js:102-171).

LMR grading quirks a server port must decide whether to preserve for parity. (a) An entirely blank board earns the crossRepresentationConsistency part, because the check is vacuously true with fewer than 2 lines (linearMultipleRepresentationsMath.js:1536-1538): 9.1% (cw/pr-1), 5.6% (pr-2) and 10% (DOL) credit for zero work, verified by running it. (b) A single trailing blank table row (from '+ Add row') fails the whole table card (validateTableEntry 1182-1184), while progress counting uses only filled rows (cardHasWork 1887). (c) Tolerances are inconsistent: slope, intercepts and the point-slope m accept 1e-4 (slope '0.3333' passes for 1/3), while the equations, table and two points require 1e-6. (d) The guided Check computes the domain key with questionData.domain ?? ctx.domain (Board.jsx:590), while the scorer uses question.domain || ctx.domain (1644).

The browser's guided per-card Check and the final submit score call the same validators with the same Graph 3 anchor resolution (Board.jsx:602-621 versus math.js:1597-1648). The browser-internal verdicts therefore agree, apart from the domain ?? versus || edge case.

The LMR browser verdict depends only on (questionData, response). The board's responseRef holds all 18 fields, and the Graph 3 anchor comes from response.pointSlopeEquation plus question.source. No hidden UI state (checkedCards, snap grids, bounds) affects the grade, so the board's existing `response` object is a sufficient raw-response contract once transported intact.

Pre-Flight (questionGenerationPreflight.js ~191) warns about device-only grading only for family-backed slots. Static registry-tool items such as all six LMR questions in docs/assignments/algebra1-linear-multiple-representations-final-v5.json, including a 1-attempt DOL, publish with no indication that they are client-graded and not deadline-finalizable.

MATHJS ALREADY DECLARED SERVER-SIDE: functions/package.json:20 declares mathjs ^15.2.0, and functions/package-lock.json:1930 locks 15.2.0, the same version as root. No functions code imports it yet. So moving linearEquations.js, algebraAstEngine.js and rewriteLinearFormMath.js into functions/shared needs no new dependency, only an exact version pin: describeRewriteGap compares simplify() output strings (rewriteLinearFormMath.js:165-176), so any mathjs version drift between browser and server changes verdicts.

BLANK WORK EARNS GRADE CREDIT (two tools, reachable with an unmodified client). (a) representationBridge linear: crossRepresentationConsistency is vacuously true when fewer than 2 student lines parse (representationBridgeMath.js:278-282). A blank submission scores 1/(stages+1): 0.167 with all 5 stages, 0.5 with a single required stage (verified). This is reachable when feedbackTiming is 'guided' or 'submitOnly' (RepresentationBridge.jsx:257-258). (b) representationMatch linearConnections group: pairwise partition scoring gives credit for unassigned cross-set pairs (representationMath.js:287-301), and 'Check groups' is never disabled (RepresentationMatch.jsx:444). Verified: blank = 48/91 = 0.527, everything in one group = 0.473. Both flow through partialCreditPercent → attemptPolicy.mjs:480-486 (capped at 90) → bestPartialCredit → getQuestionCredit (:559-563). Fix these inside the shared grader before porting, so the server does not copy the defect.

ANSWER-KEY MATERIAL IN ATTEMPT_SUBMITTED METADATA. RB: evidence.graph.anchors[].point and interceptEvidence.xIntercept.point are the true x-intercept, even for a wrong graph (constructionPolicy.js:152-164). RM: metadata.targetId (completeSet, graphMatch, findMismatch), metadata.sourceIds = mixedSet (findMismatch), and metadata.expectedId (linearConnections findMismatch, RepresentationMatch.jsx:194). Today QuestionEngine keeps only metadata.parts for ordinary assignments (QuestionEngine.jsx:756-767), and sends only payload.response under serverGrading (:744), so none of this is persisted. Any new raw-response contract must allowlist student-work fields rather than forward payload or metadata.

REPRESENTATIONMATCH GRADING IS HALF IN THE REACT COMPONENT. The sets / default-set fallback, targetId, the mixedSet fallback, the tableSpec default, tableRows ({cells} normalization and the default rows with the +2 corruption), cardKinds resolution, the expected.length===1 rules, the correction rule and the 0.6 weight are all inline in RepresentationMatch.jsx:121-139 and 181-219. Only the helpers live in representationMath.js. A node or server grader cannot reproduce the browser verdict until these are extracted into a shared module that the component also imports. By contrast, representationBridge linear is fully in representationBridgeMath.js and called directly by the component (RepresentationBridge.jsx:101).

OPAQUE ENVELOPE LIMITS. App.jsx:5677-5680 → ordinaryResponseGrading.mjs:287-292 stores JSON.stringify(response).slice(0,2000) as an opaque string; nothing on the server parses it. RB: 765 chars typical and 1858 chars for an 8-row table, and no input has a maxLength, so longer work truncates into invalid JSON. RM linearConnections group: 2411 chars for 6 sets × 10 cards. The RB response also holds nested arrays (graphConstruction.points [[x,y]]), which Firestore rejects if a contract stores the response structurally instead of as a string (firestoreAssignmentSafety.js:78-100). The contract needs object pairs.

NO DEADLINE OR DRAFT PATH FOR EITHER TOOL, though the data exists. Both tools keep full raw state in the draft at `${draftKey}:work:tool` (usePersistentToolState.js:54-72; toolStatePersistence.js:102-104, 140-149). checkpointEligibility refuses unsupported types, so no checkpoint is ever written (responseCheckpoint.js:32-39). workspaceDraftRecovery refuses the 'tool' suffix (workspaceDraftRecovery.mjs:93-101, 169-172). The draft field names differ from the emitted response names. RB: generalM/generalB/generalEquation → generalForm; graphPoints → graphConstruction.points. RM: badRow → rowIndex; linearAssignments → assignments; linearMismatchSelection → selectedId; linearCorrectionChoice → correctionChoice. A shared draft→response mapper is needed for deadline finalization and draft recovery.

RB CHECKPOINT MODE IS AN UNLIMITED, ATTEMPT-FREE VERDICT ORACLE. 'Check this stage' (RepresentationBridge.jsx:243-247 and the buttons at :413-418, 440-445, 466-471, 493-498, 553-558) shows per-stage correctness without consuming an attempt. It ignores showImmediateFeedback, which QuestionEngine sets from the activity feedback policy (QuestionEngine.jsx:192, 979). Submit is disabled until every required stage passes (:257-258). In the default 'checkpoint' timing, every submission is therefore 100% correct, even in DOL or assessment use (toolCapabilities.js:40 supportsAssessmentMode true). Server regrading would always agree, but the grade carries no assessment signal.

representationBridgeMath.js eagerly imports linearMultipleRepresentationsMath.js and re-exports it with `export *` (:26-32). Moving the linear grader to functions/shared drags the LMR module and its mathjs/algebraAstEngine graph along, unless the module is split into linear and LMR graders behind a thin dispatcher.

SOLUTION REVIEW DIVERGES FROM THE GRADER for representationMatch (toolSolutionReview.js:122-159). (1) The tableAudit review passes question.rows raw, so Firestore-safe {cells:[...]} rows (which the grader normalizes, RepresentationMatch.jsx:134-136) make every row show as 'breaks the rule', and missing function/rows are not defaulted the way the grader does. (2) There is no linearConnections branch, so it falls through to the completeSet review of sets[0].

sanitizeClientAttemptRecord trusts the client-claimed status ('correct') and partialCredit, clamped only to 0-100 rather than the 90 cap that attemptPolicy applies (submissionIngestion.mjs:476-490). For every client-verdict tool here, a modified client can record full credit; the server only bounds attempt counts and timestamps.

The browser grades presentationQuestion = generateQuestion(...) output (QuestionEngine.jsx:215-218, 253-256, 1004), not the stored question. A future server grader for these tools is only safe under the same identity-delivery gates serverGradingSupport already applies: no generator, variants or auto-differentiation, and no family template (ordinaryResponseGrading.mjs:86-97).

ALL SYSTEMS-WORKSPACE ALGEBRAIC MODES ARE CLIENT-VERDICT-SANITIZED, everywhere. In ordinary assignments, serverGradingSupport rejects the type, so gradedBy is 'client'. My Math Path has no algebraic contract. No Question Family emits systemsWorkspace: a family slot silently degrades to the `system` ordered-pair tool through questionFamilyInstance.mjs:139-145. There is no deadline checkpoint and no Recovery.

GRADED CONTRACT = A COMPLETION GATE, NOT A DISCRIMINATING CHECK. In every unique-solution mode, 'Check my work' renders only when readyToSubmit. Readiness requires every original-equation verification valid (left==right at the student's values) when requireVerification (default true), and every value comes from Step Algebra's engine-validated solved state. So an honest client can only submit isCorrect:true. In 3×3 elimination non-unique, readyToSubmit requires classified && planesEarned, and isCorrect = that same conjunction, so it is always true. The only honest wrong submission is the 2×2 degenerate special case, and that UI shows 'Correct interpretation.' live before submit (AlgebraicSystemMode.jsx:1803-1810). The 'grade' therefore records completion. Server regrading from final values adds forgery resistance (today a forged client can just claim status 'correct'), but no discrimination unless intermediate attempts are counted.

IN-TOOL FEEDBACK IGNORES THE FEEDBACK POLICY. No systemsWorkspace mode file except SystemsWorkspace.jsx imports useToolRuntimeContext or useRevealAnswers. The 2×2 special-case correctness text and green background, the plane-relationship nudges, the classification nudges, and the combination and verification checks therefore appear even when showImmediateFeedback is off (assessment or DOL). useToolSubmission suppresses only the final ResultPill.

RESPONSE IS NOT RAW STUDENT WORK FOR 3×3 NON-UNIQUE. EliminationReductionMode.jsx:282 emits classification: outcome.type, which the tool derives from checked rows and which equals the answer key whenever an outcome exists. The student's own classification choice is persisted in the draft but not emitted. The statement-kind answer ('identity'/'contradiction'/'origin') is transient useState (AlgebraicOutcome.jsx:29) and is never persisted or emitted. A naive server grader comparing response.classification to classifyLinearSystem would pass every submission.

ANSWER KEY IN SUBMIT METADATA. Every algebraic submit sends metadata.expected: solveAlgebraicSystem output for 2×2 (AlgebraicSystemMode.jsx:1228) and the full classifyLinearSystem result with solution for 3×3 (SubstitutionReductionMode.jsx:295; EliminationReductionMode.jsx:296) through onAction. QuestionEngine discards metadata except parts (QuestionEngine.jsx:756-772), so nothing is persisted, and the key is derivable from the public equations anyway. Severity is low, but any future consumer that persists metadata would store a key. The workspace draft schema forbids keys such as 'solution', 'isCorrect' and 'score' (workspaceDraftSchema.mjs:36-51), so a future raw-response contract should use `values`, not `solution`.

PATH MODE-DISPATCH DIVERGENCE / LATENT BUG. pathToolContracts.mjs dispatches on raw String(question.mode || 'linear') and treats every mode other than inequalities or matrix3 as 'linear'. The browser instead uses resolveSystemsWorkspaceMode, which overrides an explicit mode:'linear' to 'algebraic' when studentActions include solveSystem with equations (systemsWorkspaceMode.js:31-40). I verified with node that an algebraic question carrying a `system` field is Path-eligible, its public payload drops `equations`, and the browser would render AlgebraicSystemMode with the DEFAULT system x-2y=-3, 3x+5y=24 (normalizeAlgebraicSystemConfig fallback, algebraicSystemsEngine.js:497-499). The resulting {x,y} response is then rejected as malformed_response. The current seed banks contain no algebraic systemsWorkspace questions (algebra1: linear 8, inequalities 12; algebra2: matrix3 1, inequalities 14; grade8: linear 1), so this is latent. The fix is to resolve the mode with the shared resolver and make hasGradableDefinition refuse modes without a grader.

DEFAULT-SYSTEM FALLBACK HAZARD. normalizeAlgebraicSystemConfig silently substitutes ['x - 2y = -3','3x + 5y = 24'] when `equations` is missing or the wrong length. resolveSystemsWorkspaceMode still routes equationsLatex-only content to algebraic (verified: mode 'algebraic', config equations = the default pair). Authoring validation blocks this, but legacy or live content could reach students, and a server grader must refuse such content rather than mirror the fallback.

LIVE REPAIR DOWNGRADES GRADING AUTHORITY. liveResponseRepairPolicy.mjs:56-170 (SYSTEMS_WORKSPACE_UPGRADE) certifies converting a legacy `system` question (server-gradable: SERVER_GRADEABLE plus Array solution) into an algebraic systemsWorkspace (mode 'algebraic', requireVerification true). That moves those slots from server-authoritative to client-sanitized grading, and out of the checkpoint, deadline and Recovery paths.

TOLERANCE DIVERGENCE ACROSS SYSTEMS GRADERS. 2×2 algebraic uses 0.05 absolute (matchesNumericAnswer, AlgebraicSystemMode.jsx:1232-1234). 3×3 algebraic uses 1e-6 relative (substitutionReduction.js:519; EliminationReductionMode.jsx:279-280). 2×2 verification uses 0.05 absolute, 3×3 verification 1e-6 relative. Path linear systemsWorkspace uses 0.05 (pathToolContracts.mjs:641). The ordinary `system` type uses 1e-9 (ordinaryResponseGrading.mjs:159-160), and Path `system` uses numericTolerance default 1e-6. A shared grader must keep per-mode tolerances to preserve parity.

SERVER-SIDE PARSER AVAILABILITY. The answer key for every algebraic mode is derivable from public `equations` and `variables` with no stored key. The only mathjs dependency in the verdict path is equation-to-coefficients parsing (linearEquationCoefficients and linearEquationForm) and arithmetic evaluation of verification sides. functions/shared/algebraicForm.mjs (splitEquationSides, parsePolynomial, normalizeAlgebraicText) is a mathjs-free candidate, but its tokenizer lowercases and treats every letter as a separate variable (verified: parsePolynomial('2x1+3x2') gives {x:8} and '2X' gives {x:2}). It needs a parity test against linearEquationForm over all authored content, plus a refusal for multi-character or case-distinct variable names. classifyLinearSystem, solveAlgebraicSystem, planePairs, planeRelationshipTypes, KIND_FOR and matchesNumericAnswer are already pure and can move to functions/shared with src re-exports.

CLIENT STATE TRUSTED ON DRAFT REPAIR. repairReductionState keeps persisted verification checked/valid flags and back.solved.value without re-judging them (substitutionReduction.js:590-606). The 3×3 parents' `verified` conjunct therefore rests on draft-stored booleans. A server contract should carry the typed side values, not flags.

ONE SUBMIT, TWO SHAPES. AlgebraicSystemMode emits `isDegenerate ? specialCase : solution` and EliminationReductionMode emits `outcome ? {classification, statement, planes} : fullSolution`. A server grader must pick the branch from its own classifyLinearSystem or solveAlgebraicSystem result, never from the response shape, or a client could choose which rubric applies.

ENVELOPE SIZE IS NOT THE BLOCKER. All of today's algebraic responses are under 200 chars of JSON, far below the 2000-char opaque slice in normalizeOrdinaryResponse. The blockers are that kind 'opaque' is never parsed, and that the verdict depends on state not present in the response.

MODE SELECTION DIVERGES: the browser routes with resolveSystemsWorkspaceMode (systemsWorkspaceMode.js:15-55: spatial shape, algebraic intent, else mode||'linear'). Path uses String(question.mode||'linear') (pathToolContracts.mjs:616,624), and MatrixMode additionally infers matrix3 from 3x4 rows (SystemsWorkspace.jsx:1356). A shared grader must resolve mode with one pure function moved to functions/shared.

PATH FAILS OPEN FOR INEQUALITIES: normalizePathLinearInequality (pathSystemsInequalityGrading.mjs:14-20) maps any non-m/b inequality to {m:0,b:0} and any unknown relation (≤, ≥) to '>='. This rewrites BOTH the public payload the student sees and the private key, while isPathEligible stays true. The canonical engine (linearInequalityEngine.js) already handles these shapes. Current Path seed content (functions/seeds/pathQuestionBank) uses only m/b with ASCII relations, so the bug is latent but untested (tests/platform/pathSystemsInequalityGrading.test.mjs has no A/B/C, unicode or studentBuild cases).

PATH SILENTLY DOWNGRADES studentBuild/reasoning/modeling inequality questions to the legacy analyze task when they also have m/b inequalities and a testPoint (sanitizeSystemsInequalityPublicQuestion strips the flags; verified). No guard anywhere in functions/ mentions studentBuild.

DUPLICATED MATH (drift risk): solveTwoLines in toolMath.js:98-106 (nearlyEqual 1e-6) vs pathToolContracts.mjs:1103-1112 (1e-9); RREF in systemsMath.js:122-165 vs pathToolContracts.mjs:1135+; inequality evaluation in linearInequalityEngine.js vs pathSystemsInequalityGrading.mjs (m/b only). There is also a third vendored copy at functions-path-admin/vendor/shared/{pathToolContracts,pathSystemsInequalityGrading}.mjs (identical today).

SCORE POLICY DIVERGENCE: Path graded() is all-or-nothing for linear and matrix3 (pathToolContracts.mjs:403-408), while the browser gives fractional partialCreditPercent. Path's inequality grader returns the same fraction as the browser.

FREE PARTIAL CREDIT BUG: in MatrixMode, technologyCorrect = !isMatrix3 || technologyUsed (SystemsWorkspace.jsx:1385) is always true at submit (2x2 never needs technology; matrix3 returns early without it, 1378). Every matrix/matrix3 submission therefore earns at least 1/3, or 1/2 when the system has no unique solution, as partialCreditPercent in ordinary assignments.

BLANK ANSWER CREDITED: legacy InequalityMode testCorrect = (testChoice==='yes') === expectedTestPoint (SystemsWorkspace.jsx:283) treats an unanswered test point as 'no'. The studentBuild mode uses explicitBooleanAnswerMatches (457-459) correctly, and Path rejects the blank.

TOLERANCE DIVERGENCE IN REAL CONTENT: five Algebra I Path-bank linear items author numericTolerance 0.12/0.15 (e.g. mm_A_3G_v2_pricing-estimate). The browser LinearMode ignores numericTolerance (fixed 0.05).

SCHEMA-VALID CONTENT CRASHES LEGACY MODE: toolSchemas.js:147-168 accepts {orientation:'vertical', x, relation} inequalities for any inequalities question, but the legacy InequalityMode's feasibleRegionPolygon → normalizeLinearInequality throws on them (verified 'A linear inequality requires A/B/C or legacy m/b'). Only the studentBuild path maps orientation (authoredBoundaryFromInequality). Legacy construct also reads Number(ineq.m), which is NaN for A/B/C.

ALL NON-ALGEBRAIC MODES ARE CLIENT-VERDICT IN ORDINARY ASSIGNMENTS: type systemsWorkspace is not in SERVER_GRADEABLE_QUESTION_TYPES, so ingestion uses sanitizeClientAttemptRecord, which trusts the claimed status and partialCredit (submissionIngestion.mjs:480,486). A forged ordinarySubmission envelope can claim 'correct'. There is no checkpoint, deadline auto-submit, draft recovery or family Recovery for any systemsWorkspace mode.

MIGRATION IS CHEAP FOR MOST MODES: all non-rewrite graders depend only on pure, import-free modules (toolMath.js, systemsMath.js, linearInequalityEngine.js, inequalityBuilderAdapter.js). Spatial already grades with functions/shared gradeMultiAnswerResponse and needs only serverGradingSupport/'fields' plumbing. The only mathjs dependency is the studentBuild.rewrite verifier (EmbeddedInequalityRewrite.jsx), which can be rebuilt on functions/shared/algebraicForm.mjs as linearInequalityEquivalence.mjs already does.

STATE OMITTED FROM THE RESPONSE: the studentBuild verdict depends on rewriteEntries[i].verifiedConstraint and modelingSent, which are not in the submitted response (SystemsWorkspace.jsx:962-972). The studentBuild response also carries unrounded tapped floats and exceeds the 2000-char opaque slice at about 4-5 constraints (measured 2000 at 4, 2413 at 5).

ANSWER MATERIAL IN PAYLOADS: LinearMode and LinearQuadraticMode put metadata.expected (computed solution/intersections) into the ATTEMPT_SUBMITTED payload (SystemsWorkspace.jsx:119,1314), and ThreePlaneWorkspace adds metadata.classification (220). None of this is forwarded to the server, but it sits in tool feedback state. In ordinary assignments the answer keys (modeling.expectedConstraints, answerFields[].answer, expectedConstraints) are delivered to the browser because grading is client-side. The studentBuild vertex tap snaps to exact computed vertices (815-827). The spatial solutionRevealed reveal is not recorded in supportUsage.

PATH PUBLIC PAYLOADS ARE ANSWER-DERIVABLE BY DESIGN: system (linear), inequalities and matrix (matrix3) are the question, and the browser recomputes and displays the RREF solution column after the technology press (SystemsWorkspace.jsx:1414-1468). Path protects verdict authority, not answer secrecy, for these modes (pathQuestionQuality.mjs:86-104 treats them as server-derivable keys).

PATH vs BROWSER DIVERGENCE (graphing2), verified by running both graders. (1) factoredLinear is not Path-eligible: pathTargetLineFromQuestion lacks the branch. (2) A formAware question is Path-eligible but graded as equivalentLine. Example: y=2x+1 formAware with points [[1,3],[2,5]] gives browser isCorrect=false (0.667) and Path true (1.0). Example: 2x+y=4 formAware with [[1,2],[3,-2]] gives browser false and Path true. With minimumPoints 3, Path ignores the third point. (3) Partial credit for one point on the line is 0.5 in the browser and 0.333 on Path. (4) A duplicate point is a browser attempt at 0.25 but a Path reject that consumes no attempt. (5) tolerance 'abc' fails every check in the browser but becomes 0.12 on Path. The parity test (tests/platform/pathGraphingGrading.test.mjs:17-24) covers none of these.

BROWSER SCORING BUG (graphing2 constructionEvidence, graphingMath.js:77): when both points are within tolerance of the target but the constructed line is not equivalent, the result is score=1 with isCorrect=false. Verified with [[0,1.1],[0.5,1.9]] against y=2x+1. In ordinary assignments this becomes partialCreditPercent 100, capped to 90 by attemptPolicy.mjs (~480-486). It is reachable with 0.5 snapping and shallow slopes.

BROWSER GRADING BUG (functionInvestigation2): blank inputs are graded as 0 or 'none'. Number('') is 0 (FunctionInvestigation2.jsx:136-138), and parseNumericList('') returns [] (functionInvestigationMath.js:97-99). No Check button is ever disabled, and handleMissingToolAction does not gate on completeness. Verified: the parent quadratic with every field blank is marked correct; exponential k=0 with HA blank is correct; linear with anchor x blank is correct. A server port must either replicate this for parity or fix it in both places at once.

Both tools' grading math is pure and portable today: graphingMath.js, constructionPolicy.js and functionInvestigationMath.js import only src/tools/shared/toolMath.js, which has no imports. Neither needs mathjs or algebraAstEngine. The cheapest correct design is the regressionCalculator pattern: move them to functions/shared/*.mjs and turn the src files into re-exports. Note that src toolMath.round has no Number.EPSILON while pathGraphingGrading.round does, so one copy should become canonical. FI2's check logic is inline in the component (FunctionInvestigation2.jsx:135-164) and must be extracted. FI2's default-spec merge {type:'rational',a:2,h:1,k:-2,...function} (:83) and the compare defaults (:130-133) are component-level rules a server must replicate; e.g. {type:'quadratic'} gets a=2, h=1, k=-2, not 1/0/0.

ENVELOPE ALREADY SUFFICES: for both tools the ordinary envelope's opaque value is JSON.stringify(payload.response). That is under 200 chars, so it is never cut by the 2000-char slice, and it contains every input the browser verdict uses (graphing2 points; FI2 codes, parsed lists and coerced anchor). What is missing is only a server branch and a typed, bounded JSON parse. Caveats: the FI2 features anchor is Number-coerced (blank and 0 are indistinguishable; NaN becomes JSON null, which Number(null) would turn into 0), and the FI2 intercepts response holds parsed arrays rather than raw text.

ANSWER-KEY MATERIAL IN METADATA (not persisted): Graphing2 metadata carries `target` (the answer line) and, under formAware, `interceptEvidence` and anchor coordinates (Graphing2.jsx:196-205; constructionPolicy.js:152-163). This contradicts the intent of the comment at Graphing2.jsx:63-66, which says the anchor coordinate is never revealed. FI2 compare metadata carries leftValue and rightValue (:163). Today only metadata.parts is read (QuestionEngine.jsx:756-768) and Path sends only payload.response (:745), so nothing leaks. Any shared response contract should whitelist response fields and never persist metadata. graphing2's response.studentLine is derived and must be ignored server-side; Path already ignores it.

NO PER-PART EVIDENCE: neither tool emits metadata.parts, so ordinary attempts record partGrades=[] and partial credit comes only from the client score. Teachers see no point-level or field-level evidence.

LIVE CHALLENGE BUZZER GAP (all registry tools, including graphing2): registry tools are mounted with only questionData, onAction and draftKey (QuestionEngine.jsx:1003), so answerState never reflects their work. pathToolResponses BUILDERS has no graphing2 entry (pathToolResponses.js:49-92). onResponseStateChange therefore publishes null (QuestionEngine.jsx:622-628), and LiveChallengeStudent's round-end auto-submit is skipped (LiveChallengeStudent.jsx:311-316). Unchecked graphing2 work is dropped at the buzzer.

DRAFT STATE IS RICHER THAN THE ENVELOPE: both tools persist their raw state through usePersistentToolState (graphing2 'points'; FI2's 10 fields, toolStatePersistence.js:105-106). Once a shared grader exists, workspaceDraftRecovery could grade drafts. Today it refuses with unsupported-question (workspaceDraftRecovery.mjs:193-195).

FIDELITY GAPS RELEVANT TO A SERVER PORT: FI2 ignores V5-compiled analysisRequests (authoringIntentV5Core.js:1291-1301; zero references in the component) and the spec fields b and domain, which toolSchemas validates (toolSchemas.js:33-43). Authored expectations can therefore silently disagree with the derived key. For graphing2 formAware standardForm, non-lattice intercepts (for example 2x+3y=5) cannot be reached with the 0.5 snap at tol 0.12, and no schema check catches it (toolSchemas.js:539-553).

QUESTION FAMILY / RECOVERY: no family registers a graphing2 or functionInvestigation2 builder. A family slot requesting either falls back to the family defaultTool with a Pre-Flight warning (questionFamilyInstance.mjs:139-147; questionGenerationPreflight.js:184-185). Server-rebuildable family grading for these tools would need new family builders plus a graphing2/FI2 branch in gradeFamilyInstanceResponse (questionFamilyGrading.mjs:153-159).

All three tools (12 mode entries) are client-verdict-sanitized everywhere, with no server grader in any context. ordinarySubmission ingestion persists the browser's claimed status and partialCredit (submissionIngestion.mjs:476-486). Deadline auto-finalization, workspace-draft recovery, Section Recovery, Question Families and My Math Path all fail closed for these types. RESPONSE_CHECKPOINT_COMPATIBILITY.md:89 lists the registry tools as Excluded.

The extraction cost is low on the math side. transformationsMath.js and constraintFunctionMath.js depend only on src/tools/shared/toolMath.js (zero imports), and inverseCompositionMath.js and inverseDerivationMath.js have no imports at all, with no mathjs or algebraAstEngine anywhere. Suggested approach: move them to functions/shared/*.mjs and re-export from src, following src/tools/regressionCalculator/regressionCalculatorMath.js:1. Also move toolMath's nearlyEqual, round, evaluateFunctionSpec, parseNumericAnswer and matchesNumericAnswer into a shared numeric module. The real work is extracting the per-mode verdict orchestration that lives inline in the .jsx components: TransformationsLab.jsx:73-77,152-232; ConstraintFunctionBuilder.jsx:33-57,104-112; InverseCompositionLab.jsx:17-18,23-71; InverseDerivationLab.jsx:112-124.

Partial-credit bug in QuestionEngine.jsx:765-766, where object-form metadata.parts becomes equal-weight parts that include parts the mode does not grade. attemptPolicy.mjs:480-486 then records max(earnedPartPercent, supplied score). Probe results: a blank inverseCompositionLab composition-mode submit (linear f, default restrictionChoice 'none') records partialCredit 25 while the tool score is 0, and an InverseDerivationLab swap-only attempt records 50 while the tool score is 0.4. transformationsLab emits metadata.checks, which is ignored (parts = []), and constraintFunctionBuilder emits array parts consistent with its score.

Lossy emitted response in InverseCompositionLab.jsx:68. {fog: Number(fogAnswer), ...} turns blank into 0 and NaN into null, while the browser grades the raw strings, where parseNumericAnswer('') gives null and so false. Regrading today's envelope would credit blank answers whenever the expected value is 0. Raw strings must be emitted.

Answer-key exposure (security). InverseCompositionLab.jsx:69 puts metadata.expected {fog, gof, inverseAtFx, expectedRestriction} into the ATTEMPT_SUBMITTED payload and feedback state (useToolSubmission.js:9). QuestionEngine does not persist it, but any consumer that forwards metadata would leak it. More broadly, all three tools receive the full key in questionData (target and function specs, f and g, constraints) and compute verdicts locally. The constraintFunctionBuilder live checklist (ConstraintFunctionBuilder.jsx:73,176) is a per-constraint oracle shown regardless of showImmediateFeedback, even though capabilities declare supportsAssessmentMode true (toolCapabilities.js:46 overrides :35). Server grading alone will not make these secure without redacted delivery; Path does this via buildPublicToolPayload for its own tools.

Mathematical correctness bug in the InverseCompositionLab inverse part. It always expects f⁻¹(f(x)) = x (InverseCompositionLab.jsx:61), even when x lies outside a declared quadratic inverse branch. Probe: f=x², inverseBranch 'left', default x=2 accepts '2' and rejects the true value -2, which the graph plots as the 'swapped' point (192-195). Related drift: the V5 compiler stores inverseBranch at question top level and coreFunctionSpec drops it from f (authoringIntentV5Core.js:150-163,1697), but the component reads only f.inverseBranch, so branch-only V5 quadratics have canInvert=false and can never be fully correct. Also, expectedRestriction uses Number(domain.max)===h while inverseValue uses strict domain.max===h (inverseCompositionMath.js:45). A server port must decide between parity and correctness, and the browser must change in the same PR.

transformationsLab identify-mode validity: transformationParameterScore is parameter-exact and rejects graph-identical parameterizations. Probe: absolute target a=2,b=1 versus student a=1,b=2 scores 0.5 although graph score = 1, and linear a=2,h=1,k=0 versus a=2,h=0,k=-2 is rejected. Match mode, by contrast, uses graph equivalence. Untouched defaults (a=1, b=1, h=0, k=0) count toward identify partial credit, up to 75%. Hidden b (!showB) is still emitted, so a server grader should force b=1.

constraintFunctionBuilder verdict depends on the PRESENTED prompt. ConstraintFunctionBuilder.jsx:45-57 rewrites vertex constraints to vertexQuadrant when the prompt matches an English 'quadrant' regex, which duplicates the compile-time normalizeConstraintBuilderConstraints (authoringIntentV5Core.js:306-332). applyStudentSupportToQuestion swaps in translations[lang].prompt (studentSupport.js:136-141), so on legacy (non-V5) questions translated students can be graded against a different constraint set than the server's stored English prompt would yield. scoreConstraintModel also never enforces allowedFamilies (UI-only), and the hasEdited submit gate is not part of the response.

InverseDerivationLab cannot be server-verified from today's response. The verdict comes from derivation state and the operation sequence (InverseDerivationLab.jsx:66-67,112-124), but only {relation, historyLength, inverse} is emitted. Proposed contract: an operation log (max 60 entries) replayed with the pure applyInverseDerivationOperation from createLinearInverseDerivation(question.f). The drafts already hold the full derivation state, including history snapshots.

Envelope size: every response here (transformationsLab under 500 chars even for plotTransform, constraintFunctionBuilder about 200, inverseCompositionLab about 80, deriveInverse about 150) fits in the 2000-char opaque slice. None of them is a typed contract, though, and several echo question data that a grader must ignore: transformationsLab pointMap parentPoint, plotTransform sourcePoints and anchor feature, and constraintFunctionBuilder equation. normalizeOrdinaryResponse has no length guard, so truncation would silently produce unparseable JSON.

Stored versus delivered question: registry tool questions go through generateQuestion, which applies adaptive differentiation, student support (translation) and variant or generator keys (problemGenerator.js:700-745). serverGradingSupport already excludes generator, variants and auto differentiation (ordinaryResponseGrading.mjs:88-100), and the same exclusions must apply to any new tool grader. InverseCompositionLab also grades against the persisted draft x (usePersistentToolState('x'), line 29) even when the input is locked, which can diverge from question.x after a teacher edit.

For ordinary assignments, all 22 dataModelingLab, regressionCalculator, and sequenceExplorer mode entries are graded by the client. The type is absent from SERVER_GRADEABLE_QUESTION_TYPES, so ingestion stores a sanitized client record with a claimable 'correct' status (submissionIngestion.mjs:444-489, 594-603). The same Data Modeling item can grade differently on My Math Path / Live Challenge (server) and in an ordinary assignment (browser), because the two graders are separate implementations.

Path vs browser Data Modeling divergences, confirmed by running probes in node against the real client math modules and functions/shared/pathDataModelingGrading.mjs: (a) lineFit with an authored predictionX: browser requires fit+prediction, Path requires fit only; (b) the non-exploratory intercept tolerance default is a fixed 0.8 in the browser vs max(0.8,|b|*0.08) on Path, which affects live A.4C linearFitPrediction items with |b|>10; (c) Path pins an authored predictionX, while the browser lets the student move x in full and prediction modes (a browser integrity hole); (d) causationSupported is truthy vs strictly true; (e) unvalidated modelMetric and expectedModel, and uncleaned points, in the browser; (f) square-root degenerate data is always wrong in the browser but never issued on Path.

The DataModelingLab response is built with Number(rawString) (DataModelingLab.jsx:288-297). Blank inputs become 0 and fraction text becomes NaN, which is null on the wire and Number(null)=0 on the server. The browser grades the raw strings with parseNumericAnswer, so blanks are wrong. Path, reading the emitted response, can award credit for blank coefficients, r, or predictionY whenever the expected value is within tolerance of 0 (probes: quadraticFit blank b,c scores 1 on Path; blank predictionY scores prediction:true on Path). The captured fixture tests/platform/fixtures/capturedToolResponses.json already shows predictionY:0. The response contract must carry raw strings.

The Data Modeling default tolerances exist in three places: DataModelingLab.jsx:247-248 (with graphScaleService.fitAdjustmentPlan for lineFit/full), pathDataModelingGrading.mjs:253-268 and 306-317, and functions/shared/assignmentContentUpgradePolicy.mjs:44-57. The upgrade policy uses intercept 0.8 and slope max(0.2,|m|*0.12), computes the prediction tolerance from the linear regression regardless of mode, and ignores the exploratory lineFit/full tolerances. It disagrees with both graders.

Answer leak: DataModelingLab's 'Reference after submit' panel (DataModelingLab.jsx:549-551) prints the linear regression line to 2 decimals and the best-model label whenever the tool shows immediate feedback. That covers the warmup, classwork, practice, review, and corrections roles, which have 3 attempts and immediate feedback (functions/shared/activityPolicies.mjs). The fit answer (linearFit, linearFitPrediction, lineFit, full) and the modelCompare answer are revealed after attempt 1 while attempts remain. Path hides it (QuestionEngine.jsx:979).

DataModelingLab puts answer-key values in the ATTEMPT_SUBMITTED metadata: regression {m,b,r}, expectedPrediction, expectedPredictionType, expectedModel (DataModelingLab.jsx:298-305). QuestionEngine consumes only metadata.parts today, so they are not persisted, but any generic capture of payload.metadata would store the key. metadata.parts also includes all six parts regardless of mode, so ordinary partGrades show non-required parts (for example fit:false on a correlation question). This misleads teacher inspection, even though partialCredit comes from the required-part score.

RegressionCalculator processEvidence is unbounded. It records a 'tableEdited' event on every keystroke (RegressionCalculator.jsx:240-252), is never cleared (startOver appends, line 139), and is persisted as draft state. A realistic 6-row workflow serializes to about 2089 chars, past the 2000-char opaque slice, so the ordinary envelope holds truncated, invalid JSON. Process evidence should be split from the graded response.

Security: RegressionCalculator scatterplot mode hides coordinates in the UI (revealCoordinates=false), but the exact sourceData, which is the graph-to-table answer key, ships in the ordinary questionData and in the Path public payload (pathRegressionCalculatorGrading.mjs:48; the test at regressionCalculator202.test.mjs:160-165 pins this). SequenceExplorer must ship the full sequence spec (kind, first, difference/ratio) to draw its evidence, so the 'family' and 'common change' answers are always client-visible. A server-authoritative design would send only the displayed terms.

SequenceExplorer rule grading (ruleBridge, and fullBridge's writeExplicit/writeRecursive) depends on mathjs.evaluate, and functions/ has no mathjs. The server-safe evaluateExpression (functions/shared/pathQuestionGeneration.mjs:137) is not a drop-in replacement. A probe shows it parses '-2^(n-1)' as (-2)^(n-1) where mathjs gives -(2^(n-1)), and it lacks e and pi. A port needs a parity-tested evaluator.

All browser grading for these three tools lives in non-exported closures inside .jsx files (DataModelingLab check, RegressionCalculator check, and SequenceExplorer's check/matchesExplicitRule/matchesRecursiveRule/pointSetMatchesRows/inferPlotSnapStep). Node cannot import them, so tests assert source text or parity of helpers only. Extracting a pure grade(question, response) under functions/shared, and calling it from the components, is the prerequisite for both server grading and real parity tests.

Path result shape is inconsistent: gradeDataModelingResponse returns parts as an object {fit:bool,...} (pathDataModelingGrading.mjs:411-421), while the other contracts, including regressionCalculator, return [{id,isCorrect}]. submitPathResponse stores it as-is (functions/index.js:13033).

Even with a dispatcher, every authored dataModeling item (drafts/algebra1.json, algebra2.json) is legacy-generator-based, and several have variants, so serverGradingSupport would still refuse them ('generated-question'/'variant-selection'). Their instance comes from functions/shared/pathQuestionGeneration (pure, keyed by the deterministic generationKey), but src/problemGenerator.js:712-716 first runs the src-only applyAdaptiveDifferentiation, applyStudentSupportToQuestion, and selectVariant. Server rebuild of the ordinary instance, or migration to Question Families, is a separate prerequisite.

No deadline auto-finalization or Recovery exists for these tools. checkpointEligibility rejects them (no checkpoint is written), workspace draft recovery returns UNSUPPORTED_QUESTION, and Section Recovery rejects them as STATIC_QUESTION or TOOL_NOT_SERVER_GRADABLE. Work left unsubmitted at a deadline is only restorable, never graded.

None of the four tools exists anywhere under functions/: functionOperationsLab, parabolaGeometryLab, polynomialWorkshop and signSolutionAnalyzer all grep to zero hits. They are not in SERVER_GRADEABLE_QUESTION_TYPES, not in any Path CONTRACT and not in any platform question family. In every context ingestion takes the client verdict (gradedBy 'client', sanitizeClientAttemptRecord), and that function accepts the claimed status 'correct' and partialCredit (submissionIngestion.mjs:476-490).

These are among the cheapest tools to make server-authoritative. In every one of the 14 modes the browser verdict is a pure function of (questionData, emitted response): no hidden state, no history, no randomness. All the math is pure ESM with no React, DOM, mathjs or algebraAstEngine dependencies. parabola, polynomial and sign depend only on src/tools/shared/toolMath.js, which has no imports. functionOperations depends only on functions/shared/answerEquivalence.mjs. Each was verified importable in plain node. The work is: move the math modules plus toolMath's nearlyEqual, parseNumericAnswer, matchesNumericAnswer and evaluatePolynomial into functions/shared with src re-exports (the regressionCalculatorMath.js precedent), and extract each component's check() body into gradeX(question, response).

The answer-key DEFAULTS live in the JSX, not in the math modules: ParabolaGeometryLab.jsx:39,50-51,62,73; PolynomialWorkshop.jsx:47-48,68-69,98,113-114,128-131,146-149; SignSolutionAnalyzer.jsx:21,28-30,126-127; FunctionOperationsLab.jsx:41-46,52. A server grader must reproduce them byte-for-byte or it grades a different problem. This matters in practice because the V5 compiler (authoringIntentV5Core.js:1753-1767 plus copyCommon :95-116) drops polynomialWorkshop candidateRoot/leadingCoefficient/targetRoot/numeratorRoots/targetValue and parabola equidistance point/offset, so V5-authored items run on the defaults.

Security: none of the emitted responses contains answer-key material.
